SEAT
BELT
FASTENED? - The Civil
Aeronautics
Board prescribes seat belts.
Your captain will let you
know when to use the belt. His message will appear on
the electric sign above the door to his cabin.
When
the
light flashes on, fasten your belt; when it goes off, you
may loosen your belt. Here's a tip - if you'll leave
the
belt on when taking a nap, your Hostess won't have to
wake you.
PLEASE NOTE - To conform
with CAA Regulations,
all brief cases or heavy boxes must be placed on the floor.
WHAT ABOUT SMOKING?-On the ground, smoking
is not permissible in or near the plane. In the air, when
the electric sign over the pilot's
door lights up, please
heed his message - "no smoking." The rest of
smoke to your heart's content at your seat ONLY
only cigarettes, please.
You'll find ash trays on the arm
rest and by the window.
TO CLEAR YOUR EARS - As we
vary
altitude, espe-
cially when getting ready for a landing,
the pressure on
your inner
and
outer
ears
may
become
unequal.
A
healthy yawn often
will equalize the pressure,
and the
chewing gum your Hostess has for you will help too. If
you have a sinus condition or head cold, and the simpler
cures don't work, please ask your Hostess for an inhaler.
TOO HOT OR TOO COLD?-In the rack overhead
are pillows
and blankets
which your
Hostess will be
glad to hand you at any time. If you should be uncom-
fortable at any time, don't fail to give your Hostess a ring.
Know Your Crew Members
Your Skyliner captain wears two broad stripes on his sleeve.
He's in complete charge of the plane at all times. Assisting
him, is the co-pilot,
who wears one broad and one narrow
stripe on his sleeve.
On 4-engine Constellations, DC-4's and Stratoliners
we carry
an additional crew member ... a flight engineer.
He checks
instruments constantly,
relieving
but time-consuming,
duty.

You'll recognize the flight engineer
by the one broad stripe on his sleeve, and by now, you know
your TWA Hostess.
Three Tips to Aid You in
Making Return Reservations
1 - Please make your reservations requests as far
in advance as possible.
2 - Upon arrival at your stopover point, please
inform our
reservations
desk
where you'll be
staying.
It is sometimes necessary for us to con-
tact you about your return reservations.
3 - Please.
• if you can't go let us know.
If
your travel plans change, the prompt cancellation
of
your reservations will be greatly appreciated
and will help us give you better service.

YOUR MEAL IS FREE — Tasty meals are served with-
out charge if you're on a Skyliner during regular meal
hours. Fine foods, prepared and cooked in TWA's own
kitchens,
put aboard in insulated
containers.
Your
Hostess simply puts them on an attractive, one-piece tray
that's easy to manage - and dinner is served! Between-
meal
snacks
are
usually
available,
and your hostess
always has a cool drink of water for vou.
AIR TURBULENCE - Our pilot does his best to see
that we fly in smooth air, but the most skillful piloting
can't
always avoid a few
"air
bumps."
In case
you
should become nauseated suddenly, there's a removable
container clamped under your seat.
LIKE TO FRESHEN UP?-There are lavatory facilities
in the rear of the cabin. If you're traveling light, please
check with vour Hostess.
WHY THE EMPTY SEAT? — Well, it might be that the
person who reserved it had to change his plans at the
last moment and forgot to advise us.
In other words
.. a "no show." Or, it might be that our plane is carry-
ing extra gasoline, as is often the case when headwinds
are expected.
Extra fuel, like extra cargo, cuts down on
the number of passengers that can be carried.
ON READING AND WRITING - Usually, we have
the latest issue of your favorite magazines aboard.
We
also have a writing portfolio for those who want to write
or
just plain
"doodle."
It is suggested you do vour
writing with a pencil - most pens leak at high altitudes.
Please feel free to take this Souvenir Flight Packet as
a souvenir of your flight.
